title: Slow WordPress Admin (wp-admin)
description: Fix sluggish dashboard, slow post editor, and long-loading admin pages without affecting front-end performance.

steps.title: Identify Which Admin Pages Are Slow
steps.instructions: Note if all wp-admin is slow or specific screens (plugins list, post editor, WooCommerce orders). Use browser Network tab to find slow XHR requests.

steps.title: Disable Admin Bar on Front End
steps.instructions: The admin bar loads WordPress on every front-end page for logged-in users. Disable for non-admins or entirely if not needed.

steps.title: Tune or Disable Heartbeat API
steps.instructions: Frequent admin-ajax heartbeat calls slow the editor. Use Heartbeat Control plugin to limit frequency on dashboard and post edit screens.

steps.title: Audit Plugins Loading in Admin
steps.instructions: Query Monitor admin view shows per-plugin overhead. Deactivate plugins that add heavy dashboard widgets or admin notices not needed.

steps.title: Block Slow External Admin Requests
steps.instructions: Plugins checking license servers or update feeds on every admin page load cause delays. Identify via Query Monitor HTTP API calls and disable or defer.

steps.title: Enable Object Caching for Admin
steps.instructions: Redis/Memcached speeds option and meta lookups in admin too. Verify object cache drop-in is active and not misconfigured.

steps.title: Raise PHP Memory for Admin
steps.instructions: Plugin-heavy admin pages need more memory. Set WP_MAX_MEMORY_LIMIT to 512M in wp-config for admin operations.

steps.title: Verify Admin Speed Improvement
steps.instructions: Time key admin tasks: login, open post editor, save post, load plugins page. Compare before/after and document changes.
